title: Instrumented exporter diagnostics and phased phaseout plan for legacy Jaeger UDP clients
creator: Jonah Mercer
description: Problem: A small but growing cohort of customers still send spans via legacy Jaeger UDP clients. These clients bypass OTLP paths and do not honor our prefix/KV caching and backpressure heuristics, producing high packet loss during bursts and opaque failures for users. We need a solution that lets us transparently detect and instrument these legacy flows, surface backpressure diagnostics, and provide an operational phaseout plan that preserves availability.
acceptance_criteria: A sidecar translation bridge accepts legacy Jaeger UDP and emits OTLP/gRPC to the ingest layer under tenant context
Per-tenant export backpressure metrics (queue_depth, export_lag_ms, export_retries, packet_drop_estimate) are emitted to metrics pipeline and appear on dashboard panels
Automated alerts fire when exporter queue_depth > configured SLO threshold for 5m and escalate to oncall routing
Fallback routing to tempo-compatible sink occurs when primary OTLP export path rate-limits or is degraded
End-to-end e2e test demonstrating no increase in 95th percentile latency for majority of tenants during simulated legacy UDP burst (golden-run)
Runbook and phased timeline published: detection -> translation -> customer notification -> scheduled client deprecation window
tasks: Design sidecar translator: UDP listener, batch coalescer, metadata extraction, tenant mapping heuristics
Prototype metric instrumentation for translator (prometheus client): queue_depth, batches_per_sec, avg_batch_size, export_latency_ms
Add OTLP connector with retry/backoff and tempo fallback logic (configurable per-tenant)
Create dashboard panels in Console: per-tenant exporter health, queue depth heatmap, export lag histogram, legacy-client hotspots
Add e2e load test scenario to collector-harness that simulates 10k legacy UDP clients with bursty traffic
Implement canary rollout plan and feature flag gated in Dedicated and Private deployments
Write runbook, customer notification templates and support playbook
Documentation: Confluence design doc and public status/upgrade notes
comments: 2025-02-19 - Jonah Mercer: Initial scoping complete. Spike underway to validate UDP->OTLP translator performance. Targeting <50ms translation latency under 95th percentile for 512-span UDP bursts.

2025-02-24 - Aisha Kapoor: Spike shows translator CPU is dominated by JSON decode for baggage fields. Proposed optimization: move to pre-allocated buffer pool and fast path that skips baggage extraction if not present.

2025-02-26 - PK (review): Reviewed prototype. Suggest adding tenant-fingerprint heuristic (source IP + auth token hint) to avoid misattribution for NATed mobile clients. Also requested metric for 'unknown_tenant_drops'.

2025-02-28 - Aisha Kapoor: Implemented prom counters and exposed /metrics. Created initial dashboard draft: panels for queue depth, export lag, per-tenant drop rate. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/collector/pull/4823
2025-03-01 - Jonah Mercer: Ops runbook draft posted in Confluence (link below). Next: e2e harness test and canary rollout plan. Need SRE signoff on alert thresholds.
blockers: Need SRE agreement on tenant-fingerprint heuristic to avoid false positives for large NATed pools
Load-generator quota for e2e harness reserved by infra team (blocked until 2025-03-05)
notes: Plan is intentionally conservative: translation sidecar will default to a pass-through with minimal enrichment. Once we have stable metrics and dashboards, we will enable more aggressive redaction and sampling to protect storage costs before scheduling deprecation notifications.
